In factorial experiments, two or more factors are studied simultaneously, and each factor has two or more levels.

- Factorial experiments are not a design themselves, but rather a scheme that represents how treatments are arranged into experimental units.

- In factorial experiments, each level of a factor must be combined with all levels of the other factor(s) to form the complete set of treatments.

- **Main Effect:** This refers to the effect of each factor (e.g., A or B) independently of the other factors. In other words, it is the change in the response variable caused by changing the levels of a given factor.

- **Interaction Effect:** This is the combined effect of multiple factors on the response variable. Interaction occurs when the effect of the levels of one factor depends on the levels of another factor.

The model for a factorial experiment under **CRD**:
$$
Y_{ijk}=\mu+\alpha_i+\beta_j+(\alpha\beta)_{ij}+\varepsilon_{ijk}
$$
Under **RBD**:
$$
Y_{ijk}=\mu+\alpha_i+\beta_j+(\alpha\beta)_{ij}+\omega_k +\varepsilon_{ijk}
$$
Under **LSD**:
$$
Y_{ijk}=\mu+\alpha_i+\beta_j+(\alpha\beta)_{ij}+\lambda_r+\gamma_s+ +\varepsilon_{ijk}
$$

$\text{What are we testing at a factorial experiment?}$

-$H_0:$ The factors A and B are independent with respect to the response variable;

-$H_a:$  The factors A and B are NOT independent with respect to the response variable;

So, if the interaction is **not significant**, we should continue the study by analyzing the **factors independently**.

However, if the interaction turns out to be **significant**, comparisons between the levels of one factor should be made **at each level of the other factor**, since the result indicates a meaningful interaction. In other words, the effect of one factor depends on the level of the other.

## Example 1: Non-significant Interaction (CRD)

A researcher designed a factorial experiment in a Completely Randomized Design (CRD) with 5 replications to evaluate the effect of harvest time and combine type on grain loss (kg/ha). Three harvest times (H1, H2, H3) and two types of combine harvesters (T1, T2) were tested.

```{r}
rm(list=ls())
# setwd("C:/StatisticsCourse/09-Fatorial")
data <- read.table("DataColheitadeiraNS.txt", header=TRUE)

data$trat <- factor(data$trat)
data$horario <- factor(data$horario)
data$tipo <- factor(data$tipo)
data$rep <- factor(data$rep)
```

### 1. Exploratory analysis

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, paged.print=FALSE}
# install.packages("lattice")
library(lattice)
```

By harvester type

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, paged.print=FALSE}
xyplot(perda ~ horario, 
       groups = tipo, 
       data = data, jitter.x = TRUE,
       xlab = "Harvest Time", ylab = "Loss (kg/ha)", type = c("p", "a"),
       lty = c(1, 1), lwd = c(2, 2), col = c("red", "blue"),
       key = list(x = 0.02, y = 0.9, columns = 1,
                  text = list(lab = c("Type 1", "Type 2")),
                  lines = list(lty = c(1, 1), lwd = c(2, 2), col = c("red", "blue"))))
```

By harvest time

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, paged.print=FALSE}
xyplot(perda ~ tipo, 
       groups = horario, 
       data = data, jitter.x = TRUE,
       xlab = "Harvester Type", ylab = "Loss (kg/ha)", type = c("p", "a"),
       lty = 1, lwd = 2, col = c("red", "blue", "green"),
       key = list(x = 0.02, y = 0.9, columns = 1,
                  text = list(lab = c("H1", "H2", "H3")),
                  lines = list(lty = 1, lwd = 2, col = c("red", "blue", "green"))))

```

When the lines are parallel or approximately parallel, it indicates that the interaction is **not significant**.

### 2. Field layout

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, paged.print=FALSE}
source("C:/StatisticsCourse/05-DIC/ExperimentalDesignFunction.R")

set.seed(7)
field_layout(data = data,
             n_row = nrow(data)/length(levels(data$rep)),
             n_col = length(levels(data$rep)),  
             design = "CRD")$plot
```

### 3. Assumption Checks

```{r}
fit1 <- aov(data$perda ~ data$trat)
anova(fit1)
```

**1.3.1 Checking normality**

```{r}
shapiro.test(residuals(fit1))
```

**1.3.2 Checking residual homoscedasticity**

```{r}
bartlett.test(residuals(fit1) ~ data$trat)
```

### 4. Analysis of variance

```{r}
fit2 <- aov(data$perda ~ data$horario * data$tipo)
anova(fit2)
```

### 5. Multiple comparisons

Analysis using `ExpDes.pt` package for it, we can use the `fat2.dic()`
function

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, paged.print=FALSE}
library(ExpDes.pt)

fit3 <- fat2.dic(data$horario, data$tipo, data$perda, 
                 quali = c(TRUE, TRUE), 
                 mcomp = "tukey", 
                 fac.names = c("Harvest Time", "Harvester Type"),
                 sigT = 0.05, sigF = 0.05)
```

## Example 2: Non-significant Interaction (RCBD)

This is a factorial experiment arranged in a Randomized Complete Block
Design (RCBD) to evaluate the effects of two factors (A and B) on the
variable Plant Height (PH). The interaction between factors is
considered non-significant.

```{r}
rm(list=ls())

data <- read.table("DataPH.NS.txt", header=TRUE)
data$trat <- factor(data$trat)
data$bloco <- factor(data$bloco)
data$A <- factor(data$A)
data$B <- factor(data$B)
```

### 1. Exploratory analysis

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, paged.print=FALSE}
library(lattice)

xyplot(PH ~ A, 
       groups = B, 
       data = data, jitter.x = TRUE, type = c("p", "a"))
```


```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, paged.print=FALSE}
xyplot(PH ~ B, 
       groups = A, 
       data = data, jitter.x = TRUE, type = c("p", "a"))
```

### 2. Field layout

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, paged.print=FALSE}
source("C:/StatisticsCourse/05-DIC/ExperimentalDesignFunction.R")

set.seed(7)
field_layout(data = data,
             n_row = nrow(data)/length(levels(data$bloco)),
             n_col = length(levels(data$bloco)),  
             design = "DBC")$plot
```

### 3. Assumption checking

```{r}
fit1 <- aov(data$PH ~ data$trat + data$bloco)
anova(fit1)
```

**Checking normality**

```{r}
shapiro.test(residuals(fit1))
```

**Checking residual homoscedasticity**

```{r}
bartlett.test(residuals(fit1) ~ data$trat)
```

### 4. Analysis of variance

```{r}
fit2 <- aov(data$PH ~ data$bloco + data$A * data$B)
anova(fit2)

model.tables(fit2, type = "means")
```

### 5. Multiple comparisons

```{r}
library(ExpDes.pt)

fit3 <- fat2.dbc(data$A, data$B, data$bloco, data$PH,
                 quali = c(TRUE, TRUE),
                 mcomp = "tukey",
                 fac.names = c("A", "B"),
                 sigT = 0.05, sigF = 0.05)
```

## Example 3: Significant Interaction (CRD)

A factorial experiment was conducted using a Completely Randomized
Design (CRD) to evaluate the effect of two factors --- Container and
Species --- on seedling height at 80 days of age.

**Container levels:**

-   Small plastic bag (R1)

-   Large plastic bag (R2)

-   Laminated bag (R3)

**Species levels:**

-   *Eucalyptus citriodora* (E1)

-   *Eucalyptus grandis* (E2)

```{r}
rm(list=ls())
data <- read.table("DataSignif.txt", header=TRUE)
data$trat <- factor(data$trat)
data$R <- factor(data$R)
data$E <- factor(data$E)
data$rep <- factor(data$rep)

knitr::kable(data)
```

### 1. Exploratory analysis

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, paged.print=FALSE}
library(lattice)
```

By repetition within each species
```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, paged.print=FALSE}
xyplot(alt ~ R | E, 
       groups = rep, 
       data = data, 
       layout = c(2,1), jitter.x = TRUE,
       xlab = "Containers", 
       xlab.top = "Species", 
       ylab = "Height (cm)", pch = 16,
       lwd = c(2,2,2,2), col = c(1,2,3,4),
       key = list(x = 0.02, y = 0.3, columns = 1,
                  text = list(lab = c("R1","R2","R3","R4")),
                  lwd = 2, col = c(1,2,3,4)))
```

By species
```{r}
xyplot(alt ~ R, 
       groups = E, 
       data = data, 
       jitter.x = TRUE, 
       xlab = "Containers",
       ylab = "Height (cm)", 
       type = c("p", "a"),
       lty = c(1,1), lwd = c(2,2), 
       col = c("red","blue"),
       key = list(x = 0.02, y = 0.3, columns = 1,
                  text = list(lab = c("E1","E2")),
                  lines = list(lty = c(1,1), 
                               lwd = c(2,2), 
                               col = c("red","blue"))))
```

By container
```{r}
xyplot(alt ~ E, 
       groups = R, 
       data = data, 
       jitter.x = TRUE, 
       xlab = "Species",
       ylab = "Height (cm)", 
       type = c("p", "a"),
       lty = c(1,1,1), lwd = c(2,2,1), 
       col = c("red","blue","green"),
       key = list(x = 0.02, y = 0.3, columns = 1,
                  text = list(lab = c("R1","R2","R3")),
                  lines = list(lty = c(1,1,1), 
                               lwd = c(2,2,1), 
                               col = c("red","blue","green"))))

```

When the lines are **not** parallel or approximately parallel, it indicates that the interaction is **significant**.

### 2. Field layout
```{r}
source("C:/StatisticsCourse/05-DIC/ExperimentalDesignFunction.R")

set.seed(7)
field_layout(data = data,
             n_row = nrow(data)/length(levels(data$rep)),
             n_col = length(levels(data$rep)),  
             design = "DIC")$plot
```

### 3. Assumption Checking
```{r}
fit1 <- aov(data$alt ~ data$R * data$E)
anova(fit1)
```

**3.3.1 Checking normality**
```{r}
shapiro.test(residuals(fit1))
```

**3.3.2 Checking residual homoscedasticity**
```{r}
bartlett.test(residuals(fit1) ~ data$trat)
```

### 4. ANOVA - Interaction effect
```{r}
fit2 <- aov(data$alt ~ data$E * data$R)
anova(fit2)

model.tables(fit2, type = "means", se = TRUE)
```

### 5. Multiple comparison
```{r}
library(ExpDes.pt)

fit3 <- fat2.dic(data$R, 
                 data$E, 
                 data$alt, 
                 quali = c(TRUE, TRUE), mcomp = "tukey",
                 fac.names = c("Containers", "Species"),
                 sigT = 0.01, sigF = 0.01)
```
